checks: Matched 641c5559a440bf48 §1 (1) and 0b2178fc42ce31d4 §1. The latter uses a half-mass coupling and doubles its image; the frozen unit-mass coupling with doubled marginals gives exactly that image law.

The median conditions make both proportional assignments nonnegative and their sum the central mass. If the central mass is zero, both assignments are zero. The support sets and the compact median fiber are actual, including the case of no original mass on that fiber.

The interpolation coefficients are nonnegative and sum to one, and allow zero weight when one endpoint is already at the median. At a pair with both bases equal to the median the midpoint is legal. Integer base-pair strata are clopen, so the map is continuous on the legal pair product.

Both endpoints outside a closed halfspace place their entire segment in its open convex complement, proving the indicator inequality even at charged target boundaries. Integration uses the sum 2μ of the two marginals. Whole-fiber traces from vertical containing caps have full target mass.

overlap.comparison: Uses the same elementary endpoint indicator for arithmetic same-parity product midpoints and preserves the barycenter in that construction. The frozen law uses a single prescribed median base, distance-dependent coefficients and arbitrary couplings of its two prescribed half-marginals.
Works with swap-symmetric parity product couplings and cap/base conditioning. Those fixed parity and midpoint conditions do not give the arbitrary median interpolation law.

readability: The normalization differs from the source’s half-mass coupling only by multiplying the coupling itself by two.
review_method: Independent cold proof read of the exact frozen statement and proof, original locator comparison, predecessor verification, and exact arithmetic where applicable.
summary: Every legal median-segment coupling gives the claimed factor-two closed-halfspace domination.
